resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's own current_ref (https://www.cheniere.com/where-we-work/cc-pipeline) is confirmed DEAD -- HTTP 404 via scripts/url_verifier.py -- so this is DEAD_LINK-eligible, but a working Wayback capture of the identical page exists and is proposed as the replacement (a confirmed-dead origin, not merely a blocked one, so swapping in the archived capture is appropriate rather than leaving the cell empty). That August 2025 capture (publisher: Cheniere Energy) states: 'Quick facts... In service: 2018' and describes the pipeline as an operating 21.5-mile, 48-inch line delivering feed gas to the Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility. Independently, FERC's own March 2019 Environmental Assessment for the Stage 3 Project (hosted at energy.gov; publisher: FERC/DOE) repeatedly refers to 'the recently completed Corpus Christi Pipeline' (Docket No. CP12-508-000) and its project-inventory table lists the 'Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline LP' 48-inch pipeline with a 2015-2018 construction period. Cheniere's own FY2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filer Cheniere Corpus Christi Holdings LLC) independently confirms it was placed in operation ('construction... was completed in the second quarter of 2018'). Two distinct publishers (Cheniere; FERC/DOE) agree the line is complete and operating.

Cheniere's project page (Wayback capture, replacing the confirmed-dead cheniere.com live URL) describes it as 'a 21.5-mile, 48-inch natural gas pipeline' designed 'to transport 2.75 Bcf/d of feed gas.' FERC's Stage 3 EA (a document authored and published by FERC, a distinct publisher from Cheniere) repeatedly calls it a 'bi-directional interstate natural gas pipeline' and describes the interconnecting Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Transcontinental Gas Pipeline, etc., as natural-gas systems. Two distinct publishers agree the commodity is natural gas.

FERC's Stage 3 EA states the original Corpus Christi Pipeline was 'the 48-inch-diameter pipeline approved by the Commission in Docket No. CP12-508-000' -- a Section 7(c) Natural Gas Act certificate, the definitional marker of an interstate gas transmission line. Cheniere's own FY2018 10-K (SEC EDGAR) independently states: 'In December 2014, the FERC issued a certificate of public convenience and necessity under Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act... authorizing CCP to construct and operate the Corpus Christi Pipeline,' and separately that 'the transportation of natural gas through the Corpus Christi Pipeline' falls under FERC's NGA jurisdiction over 'interstate commerce.' Two distinct publishers (FERC; Cheniere) agree it is an NGA-certificated interstate transmission pipeline.

Cheniere's FY2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR) states explicitly: 'The construction of the Corpus Christi Pipeline commenced in January 2017 and was completed in the second quarter of 2018.' FERC's Stage 3 EA project-inventory table independently lists the 'Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline LP' 48-inch pipeline's construction period as '2015 - 2018' and elsewhere calls it the 'recently completed Corpus Christi Pipeline' as of its March 2019 publication. Cheniere's own current project page (Wayback capture) also lists 'In service: 2018' as a quick fact. Two distinct publishers (Cheniere; FERC) agree on a 2018 in-service year, matching the sheet's StartYear1/StartYear2 (2018).

CONCERN: extensive search did not turn up any source stating a $500 million cost for the Corpus Christi Pipeline, and the primary-source figures I did find are all materially lower and consistent with each other. Cheniere/Corpus Christi Pipeline GP's SEC Form S-4 (filed 2017-01-05, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693317/000119312517002987/d322026ds4.htm): 'total target contract price of constructing the Corpus Christi Pipeline based on our CCP Construction Contracts is approximately $130 million. We estimate that the total expected capital costs for the Corpus Christi Pipeline will be between $350 million and $450 million.' The FY2017 10-K (filed 2018-02-21, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693317/000169331718000002/cch2017form10-k.htm) narrowed this to 'estimated capital costs for the Corpus Christi Pipeline of between $350 million and $400 million.' The FY2019 10-K's audited financial statements (Note on Property, Plant and Equipment, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693317/000169331720000003/cch2019form10k.htm) show actual capitalized 'Total natural gas pipeline costs' of $375.1 million (as of Dec 31, 2018) and $397.7 million (as of Dec 31, 2019, including land and construction-in-process), consistent with the pre-construction estimate range and well short of $500 million. The Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Ongoing Projects' report (PN1018, Oct 2018) lists length/diameter/location/contractor for the project but no cost figure. Searched Natural Gas Intel, FracTracker, and general trade press for a $500 million figure via curl/API-based search (WebSearch quota was exhausted this session; Bing, DuckDuckGo-html, and Mojeek scraping via curl all returned blocked/empty results) and found nothing repeating $500M. Given the sheet's own audited-cost sources consistently land in the $350-400M actual/estimated range, the $500M figure on the sheet may be a data issue (possibly conflating with a different Cheniere Corpus Christi project cost, or a stale/rounded estimate) -- flagging for Update rather than changing the value or fabricating a citation for it.
